detailed_summary: This paper reports the synthesis of isotopically purified planar germanium (Ge) two-dimensional hole gases (2DHGs) using enriched 70GeH4 precursor, and demonstrates significant improvements in hole spin qubit coherence times and gate fidelities. The authors show that by suppressing nonzero-spin 73Ge nuclei, the qubit dephasing time T2* at the sweet spot is extended beyond 20 μs, surpassing previous Ge hole qubit records. More importantly, off the sweet spot, T2* is enhanced to above 3 μs, enabling single-qubit gate fidelities exceeding 99.9% in both operating regimes. Hahn-echo spectroscopy reveals a finite-frequency nuclear-noise channel distinct from conventional Larmor-linked hyperfine response, which is attributed to quadrupole-modified dynamics of residual 73Ge nuclei near the Ge/SiGe interface. The field scaling and angle-dependent visibility of this noise are consistent with a qubit-visible quadrupolar nuclear-noise component transduced through the anisotropic hyperfine interaction of Ge holes. These results establish isotopically purified planar Ge as a high-coherence scalable platform for hole spin qubits and provide a spectroscopic probe of interfacial quadrupolar nuclear dynamics.
key_contributions: Demonstration of isotopically purified planar Ge 2DHG with enriched 70GeH4 precursor, achieving suppression of nuclear spin noise.
Extension of qubit T2* beyond 20 μs at the sweet spot and above 3 μs off the sweet spot, enabling single-qubit gate fidelities >99.9%.
Identification of a finite-frequency nuclear-noise channel via Hahn-echo spectroscopy, distinct from Larmor-linked hyperfine response.
Attribution of the new noise channel to quadrupole-modified dynamics of residual 73Ge nuclei near the Ge/SiGe interface.
Establishment of isotopically purified planar Ge as a scalable high-coherence platform for hole spin qubits.
methodology_analysis: The authors synthesized isotopically purified 2DHGs using chemical vapor deposition with enriched 70GeH4 precursor, which reduces the concentration of nonzero-spin 73Ge nuclei. They fabricated hole spin qubits in planar Ge quantum wells and characterized coherence times using Ramsey interferometry (T2*) and Hahn-echo spectroscopy. Gate fidelities were estimated from randomized benchmarking. The nuclear-noise channel was probed by measuring the echo decay as a function of interpulse delay, revealing a finite-frequency component. The authors compared experimental data with theoretical models of quadrupolar nuclear dynamics, including field scaling and angle-dependent visibility, to support their interpretation.
results_analysis: The key results include: (1) T2* at the sweet spot exceeds 20 μs, a significant improvement over previous Ge hole qubits (typically <10 μs). (2) Off the sweet spot, T2* is >3 μs, enabling >99.9% single-qubit gate fidelity in both regimes. (3) Hahn-echo spectroscopy reveals a noise peak at finite frequency (∼10-100 kHz) that scales with magnetic field and shows angle dependence, consistent with quadrupolar nuclear dynamics. The authors quantify the noise suppression factor due to isotopic purification and show that residual 73Ge nuclei still contribute via quadrupolar interactions. The results demonstrate that isotopic purification effectively reduces hyperfine noise but reveals a new noise source from interfacial quadrupolar effects.
strengths: Clear demonstration of improved coherence times and gate fidelities through isotopic purification, with quantitative benchmarks.
Identification and characterization of a new nuclear-noise channel using advanced spectroscopy techniques (Hahn-echo).
Strong theoretical support for the quadrupolar origin of the noise, including field scaling and angle dependence.
Practical relevance for scalable quantum computing in Ge-based platforms.
limitations: The study focuses on single-qubit performance; two-qubit gate fidelities and scalability remain to be demonstrated.
The quadrupolar noise channel may impose a fundamental limit on coherence even with full isotopic purification.
The paper does not provide detailed statistics on qubit-to-qubit variation or yield across the wafer.
connections_to_research: This work directly advances quantum physics research in spin-based quantum computing, particularly in group-IV semiconductors. It addresses the critical issue of nuclear spin noise in hole qubits, a key challenge in quantum information processing. The use of isotopic purification and the discovery of quadrupolar nuclear dynamics provide new insights into decoherence mechanisms, relevant to both fundamental quantum physics and practical qubit engineering. The results are directly applicable to the development of scalable quantum processors in Ge platforms.
overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant advance in Ge hole spin qubits by demonstrating the benefits of isotopic purification and uncovering a new quadrupolar nuclear noise channel. The coherence times and gate fidelities achieved are state-of-the-art for Ge qubits, and the spectroscopic identification of the noise source is a valuable contribution. The work is technically sound, well-supported by theory, and has clear implications for scalable quantum computing. It is a high-quality paper that will influence future research in semiconductor spin qubits.
